subject.title: [Bug]: Block streaming can drop paragraph separators across streamed updates

question: Should OpenClaw preserve consumed paragraph separators in-band on emitted chunks, or require explicit boundary metadata before landing a closing PR?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible, but the permanent boundary contract affects shared block-streaming delivery and two open PRs already propose the in-band separator approach.

options.title: Land one in-band separator fix
options.body: Review and consolidate one linked PR that carries the paragraph separator on emitted chunks and prevents coalescer double-joining.

options.title: Require boundary metadata
options.body: Pause the linked PRs until a metadata-carrying boundary contract is designed and tested through delivery.

options.title: Reject current fix direction
options.body: Close or pause the candidate PRs and leave this issue open for a future maintainer-sponsored design.

recommendation.title: Land one in-band separator fix
recommendation.body: Review and consolidate one linked PR that carries the paragraph separator on emitted chunks and prevents coalescer double-joining.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the paragraph-boundary streaming semantics and authored the follow-up most closely tied to the current boundary-loss behavior.
